exampleAnswers.title: Finding a Marginal CDF Using a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for $ (x,y) \in [0,1] \times [0,1],$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= 2^{xy}-1. \]

Find $F_X(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

\[ F_X(x) = F(x,\infty) = \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} F(x,y). \]

Therefore, for $0\leq x\leq 1,$ we have

\begin{align} F_X(x) &= F(x,\infty) \\[5pt] &= F(x,1) \\[5pt] &= 2^{x(1)}-1\\[5pt] &= 2^x-1. \end{align}

example.title: Finding a Marginal CDF Using a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{x(y^2-1)}{y^2(x+3)}, & {x \geq 0,\; y \geq 1}\\[5pt] 0, & x \lt 0 \; \textrm{or} \; y \lt 1. \end{cases} \]

Find $F_X(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $x \geq 1.$
question.explanation:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

\[ F_X(x)= F(x,\infty) = \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} F(x,y). \]

Therefore, for $x \geq 0,$ we have

\begin{align} F_X(x) &= \lim_{y \to \infty} \left(\dfrac{x(y^2-1)}{y^2(x+3)}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x}{x+3} \lim_{y \to \infty} \left(\dfrac{y^2-1}{y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x}{x+3} \lim_{y \to \infty} \left(1-\dfrac{1}{y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x}{x+3} \lim_{y \to \infty} \left(1-0\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x}{x+3}. \end{align}

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for $ (x,y) \in [0,1] \times [0,2],$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \dfrac{x^3y}{2}. \]

Find $F_X(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

\[ F_X(x) = F(x,\infty) = \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} F(x,y). \]

Therefore, for $0\leq x\leq 1,$ we have

\begin{align} F_X(x) &= F(x,\infty) \\[5pt] &= F(x,2) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^3(2)}{2} \\[5pt] &= x^3. \end{align}

example.title: Finding a Marginal CDF Using a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} 0, & {x \lt 0\;\textrm{or}\; y \lt 0}\\[5pt] \dfrac{x^2 \arctan y}{2\pi}, & {0 \leq x \leq 2,\; y \geq 0} \\[5pt] F_Y(y), & x > 2, \; y \geq 0. %\dfrac{\arctan y}{2\pi} . \end{cases} \]

Find $F_X(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2.$
question.explanation:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

\[ F_X(x)= F(x,\infty) = \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} F(x,y). \]

Therefore, for $0 \leq x \leq 2,$ we have

\begin{align} F_X(x) &= \lim\limits_{y \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{x^2 \arctan y}{2\pi}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^2}{2\pi} \cdot \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} \arctan y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{x^2}{2\pi} \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}x^2 . \end{align}

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y,$ for $ (x,y) \in [0,1] \times [0,2],$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \dfrac{1}{20}x^2y(4x+3y). \]

Find $F_X(x),$ the marginal CDF of $X,$ for $0 \leq x \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
The marginal CDF of $X$ is given by

\[ F_X(x) = F(x,\infty) = \lim\limits_{y \to \infty} F(x,y). \]

Therefore, for $0\leq x\leq 1,$ we have

\begin{align} F_X(x) &= F(x,\infty) \\[5pt] &= F(x,2) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{20}x^2(2)(4x+3(2)) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{10}x^2(4x+6) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{5}(2x^3+3x^2). \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding Part of a Joint CDF from Marginal CDFs for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

\[ F_X(x) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}, & x\geq 1 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad\qquad F_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{1}{y}, & y\geq 1 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $x \geq 1$ and $y\geq 1.$
question.explanation:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs $F_X(x)$ and $F_Y(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

\[ F(x,y) = F_X(x) \cdot F_Y (y). \]

Therefore, for $x \geq 1$ and $y \geq 1,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is

\begin{align} F(x,y) &=F_X(x)\cdot F_Y (y) \\[5pt] &=\left(1-\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{1}{y}\right) \\[5pt] &=1-\dfrac{1}{x^2} -\dfrac{1}{y}+\dfrac{1}{x^2y}. \end{align}

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

\[ F(x,y) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{1}{x^2} -\dfrac{1}{y}+\dfrac{1}{x^2y}, & x\geq 1,\; y\geq 1\\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

question.text:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

\[ F_X(x) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{16}{x^4}, & x\geq 2 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad\qquad F_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{8}{y^3}, & y\geq 2 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $x \geq 2$ and $y\geq 2.$
question.explanation:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs $F_X(x)$ and $F_Y(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

\[ F(x,y) = F_X(x) \cdot F_Y (y). \]

Therefore, for $x \geq 2$ and $y \geq 2,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is

\begin{align} F(x,y) &=F_X(x)\cdot F_Y (y) \\[5pt] &=\left(1-\dfrac{16}{x^4}\right)\left(1-\dfrac{8}{y^3}\right) \\[5pt] &=1-\dfrac{16}{x^4}-\dfrac{8}{y^3}+\dfrac{128}{x^4y^3}. \end{align}

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

\[ F(x,y) = \begin{cases} 1-\dfrac{16}{x^4}-\dfrac{8}{y^3}+\dfrac{128}{x^4y^3}, & x\geq 2,\; y\geq 2\\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Finding Part of a Joint CDF from Marginal CDFs for Continuous Random Variables

question.text:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

\[ F_X(x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x< 0 \\[3pt] x, & 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\[3pt] 1, & x > 1 \end{cases} \qquad\qquad F_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 0, & y< 0 \\[3pt] y, & 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[3pt] 1, & y > 1 \end{cases} \]

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $ 0\leq x \leq 1$ and $0\leq y \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs $F_X(x)$ and $F_Y(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

\[ F(x,y) = F_X(x) \cdot F_Y (y). \]

Therefore, for $0\leq x \leq 1$ and $0\leq y \leq 1,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is

\begin{align} F(x,y) &=F_X(x)\cdot F_Y (y) \\[5pt] &=x \cdot y \\[5pt] &=xy. \end{align}

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is \[ F(x,y) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \textrm{ or } y< 0 \\[5pt] xy, & 0 \leq x \leq 1,\;0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] x, & 0 \leq x \leq 1,\; y > 1 \\[5pt] y, & x > 1,\; 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 1, & x > 1,\; y > 1 \end{cases} \]

question.text:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

\[ F_X(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{2+x}, & x\geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad\qquad F_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 1-e^{-2y}, & y\geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $x \geq 0$ and $y\geq 0.$
question.explanation:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs $F_X(x)$ and $F_Y(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

\[ F(x,y) = F_X(x) \cdot F_Y (y). \]

Therefore, for $x \geq 0$ and $y \geq 0,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is

\begin{align} F(x,y) &=F_X(x)\cdot F_Y (y) \\[5pt] &=\left(\dfrac{x}{2+x}\right)\left(1-e^{-2y}\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{x}{2+x}\left(1-e^{-2y}\right). \end{align}

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

\[ F(x,y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{x}{2+x}\left(1-e^{-2y}\right), & x\geq 0,\; y\geq 0\\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

question.text:
The marginal CDFs of two continuous independent random variables $X$ and $Y$ are given below.

\[ F_X(x) = \begin{cases} 1-e^{-6x}, & x\geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \qquad\qquad F_Y(y) = \begin{cases} 1-e^{-y/3}, & y\geq 0 \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Find the expression for the joint CDF when $x \geq 0$ and $y\geq 0.$
question.explanation:
If $X$ and $Y$ are independent continuous random variables with marginal CDFs $F_X(x)$ and $F_Y(y),$ respectively, then the corresponding joint CDF of $F(x,y)$ is given by

\[ F(x,y) = F_X(x) \cdot F_Y (y). \]

Therefore, for $x \geq 0$ and $y \geq 0,$ the joint CDF for our random variables is

\begin{align} F(x,y) &=F_X(x)\cdot F_Y (y) \\[5pt] &=(1-e^{-6x})(1-e^{-y/3}) \\[5pt] &=1-e^{-y/3}-e^{-6x}+e^{-6x-y/3}. \end{align}

Therefore, the full expression for the joint CDF is

\[ F(x,y) = \begin{cases} 1-e^{-y/3}-e^{-6x}+e^{-6x-y/3}, & x\geq 0,\; y\geq 0\\[5pt] 0, &\textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Recovering the Joint PDF from a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{(x-1)(y-1)}{xy}, & x \geq 1, \; y \geq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $x \geq 1$ and $y \geq 1.$
question.explanation:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is given by \[ f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y). \]

For $x \geq 1$ and $y \geq 1,$ we have \begin{align} f(x,y) & = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x\partial y} F(x,y) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{(x-1)(y-1)}{xy} \right) \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{x-1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( 1- \dfrac{1}{y} \right) \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{x-1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{y^2} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{y^2} \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{x} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{y^2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x^2} \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x^2 y^2}. \end{align}

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$

Therefore, we have \[ f(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{x^2 y^2}, & x \geq 1, \; y \geq 1\\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Recovering the Joint PDF from a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} 0, & x \lt -1 \; \textrm{or} \; y \lt 0 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}(x^3 + 1)y^2, & -1 \leq x \leq 1, \; 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] F_X(x), & -1 \leq x \leq 1, \; y > 1 \\[5pt] F_Y(y), & x > 1, \; 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 1, & x \gt 1, \; y \gt 1. \end{cases} \]

where $F_X$ and $F_Y$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $-1 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1.$
question.explanation:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is determined by \[ f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y). \]

For $-1 \leq x \leq 1$ and $0 \leq y \leq 1,$ we have \begin{align} f(x,y) & = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x\partial y} F(x,y) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{1}{2}(x^3 + 1)y^2 \right)\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{1}{2}(x^3 + 1) \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( y^2 \right)\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{1}{2}(x^3 + 1) \cdot 2y \right) \\[5pt] & = y \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( x^3 + 1 \right) \\[5pt] & = y \cdot 3x^2\\[5pt] & = 3x^2 y. \end{align}

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$ Therefore, we have \[ f(x,y)= \begin{cases} 3x^2 y, & -1 \leq x \leq 1, \; 0 \leq y \leq 1 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Recovering the Joint PDF from a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} 0, & {x \lt 1\textrm{ or } y \lt 1} \\[5pt] \dfrac{4(x^2-1)(y-1)}{9y}, & {1 \leq x \leq 2,\; 1 \leq y \leq 4} \\[5pt] F_X(x), & {1 \leq x \leq 2,\; y > 4} \\[5pt] F_Y(y), & { x > 2,\; 1 \leq y \leq 4} \\[5pt] 1, & {x \gt 2,\; y \gt 4}. \end{cases} \]

where $F_X$ and $F_Y$ are the marginal CDFs of $X$ and $Y,$ respectively. Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $1 \leq x \leq 2$ and $1 \leq y \leq 4.$
question.explanation:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is determined by

\[ f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y). \]

For $1 \leq x \leq 2$ and $1 \leq y \leq 4,$ we have

\begin{align} f(x,y) &= \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x\partial y} F(x,y) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left(\dfrac{4(x^2-1)(y-1)}{9y}\right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( 4(x^2-1) \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left(\dfrac19 - \dfrac{1}{9y}\right)\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( 4(x^2-1) \cdot \dfrac{1}{9y^2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4}{9y^2} \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(x^2-1\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{8x}{9y^2}. \end{align}

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$ Therefore, we have

\[ f(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{8x}{9y^2}, & {1 \leq x \leq 2,\; 1 \leq y \leq 4} \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Recovering the Joint PDF from a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by \[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{(x-1)(e^{y}-1)}{xe^{y}}, & x \geq 1, \; y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $x \geq 1,\, y \geq 0.$
question.explanation:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is given by \[ f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y). \]

For $x \geq 1$ and $y \geq 0,$ we have \begin{align} f(x,y) & = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x\partial y} F(x,y) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( \dfrac{(x-1)(e^{y}-1)}{xe^{y}} \right) \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{x-1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} \left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{e^{y}} \right) \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \dfrac{x-1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{1}{e^y} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{e^y} \cdot \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( 1 - \dfrac{1}{x} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{e^{y}} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x^2}\\[5pt] & = \dfrac{1}{x^2 e^y}. \end{align}

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$

Therefore, we have \[ f(x,y)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{x^2 e^{y}}, & x \geq 1, \, y \geq 0 \\[5pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

example.title: Recovering the Joint PDF from a Joint CDF

question.text:
The joint CDF of two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given by

\[ F(x,y)= \begin{cases} (1-e^{-x})(1-e^{-y}), & {x \geq 0,\; y \geq 0} \\[5pt] 0, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]

Find the joint PDF $f(x,y)$ for $x\geq 0,\, y\geq 0.$
question.explanation:
Since the partial derivatives of $F(x,y)$ are defined, the joint probability density function $f(x, y)$ is given by

\[ f(x,y) = \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x \partial y} F(x,y). \]

For $x\geq0$ and $y\geq0,$ we have

\begin{align} f(x,y) &= \dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial x\partial y} F(x,y) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left(\dfrac{\partial}{\partial y} (1-e^{-x})(1-e^{-y})\right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial}{\partial x} \left((1-e^{-x})(e^{-y})\right) \\[5pt] &= e^{-x-y}. \end{align}

Otherwise, $f(x,y) = 0.$

Therefore, we have

\[ f(x,y)= \begin{cases} e^{-x-y}, & {x\geq 0,\, y\geq 0} \\[3pt] 0, & \textrm{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]
